summary: Defines the UIDPLUS extension to IMAP4, which gives clients features that reduce the time and resources used by some operations, particularly around unique message identifiers. It was replaced by RFC 4315.

plainLanguage.summary: A shortcut that lets your email program ask for exact message numbers instead of searching through a whole mailbox.

questions: how does uidplus help offline email clients
subtitle: Three protocol optimizations that let email clients work more efficiently with IMAP servers.

tldr.problem: IMAP4 clients that work offline need to minimize round trips to the server when managing messages, especially when expunging or copying messages identified by unique IDs.
tldr.mechanism: UIDPLUS adds three features: a UID EXPUNGE command that deletes specific messages by ID, and two response codes (APPENDUID and COPYUID) that return the UIDs of appended and copied messages so clients do not have to query the server again.
tldr.outcome: The extension provided important optimizations for disconnected IMAP clients, though it was replaced by RFC 4315 which consolidated IMAP extensions.

today: RFC 2359 was a Proposed Standard and was replaced by RFC 4315, which consolidated IMAP4 extensions. The UIDPLUS features remain useful for IMAP implementations that support offline clients.

sections.title: The UIDPLUS Extension
sections.content:
UIDPLUS is an extension to the Internet Message Access Protocol version 4 (IMAP4). The extension provides features intended to reduce the time and resources used by client operations, particularly for clients that work in disconnected mode.

An IMAP4 server advertises support for UIDPLUS by returning UIDPLUS in response to a CAPABILITY command. The extension adds one new command and additional response codes that servers return with successful APPEND and COPY commands. Clients can provide the same functionality without UIDPLUS by using other IMAP4 commands, but more slowly.
sections.plainLanguage: IMAP is a protocol that lets your email program talk to a mail server to get messages. UIDPLUS is an add-on that gives the server a way to tell your program faster results when your program asks to add or move messages.

sections.title: The UID EXPUNGE Command
sections.content:
The UID EXPUNGE command permanently removes messages from the currently selected mailbox. Unlike the standard EXPUNGE command, UID EXPUNGE only deletes messages that both have the \Deleted flag set and have a UID (unique identifier) that is included in the specified message set.

This is useful for disconnected clients. When a user marks messages for deletion offline and the mailbox changes before the expunge is replayed to the server, UID EXPUNGE ensures the client only deletes the intended messages. If other messages were marked for deletion in the meantime, they are not affected.

Without UIDPLUS, a client would have to use the STORE command to remove the \Deleted flag from unwanted messages before calling EXPUNGE, or take the risk that EXPUNGE might delete unintended messages.
sections.plainLanguage: The UID EXPUNGE command is like saying to the mail server: delete the messages I sent you, and only those messages, rather than delete all messages marked for deletion. This is safer when the server has changed since your last check.

sections.title: APPENDUID Response
sections.content:
When a client appends a new message to a mailbox, the APPENDUID response code tells the client the UID that the server assigned to the new message. The response contains two pieces of information: the UIDVALIDITY value of the destination mailbox and the UID of the appended message.

Without this response, a client would have to select the mailbox and issue FETCH commands to discover which UID the server assigned to the new message. With APPENDUID, the server returns this information immediately with the OK response, saving a round trip.

Example: A003 OK [APPENDUID 38505 3955] APPEND completed tells the client that the message was assigned UID 3955 in a mailbox with UIDVALIDITY 38505.
sections.plainLanguage: When you send a new message to the mail server, the server automatically gives it a number. APPENDUID makes the server tell you the number right away, so you do not have to ask the server a second time.

sections.title: COPYUID Response
sections.content:
When a client copies one or more messages to another mailbox, the COPYUID response code provides three pieces of information: the UIDVALIDITY of the destination mailbox, the UIDs of the messages copied from the source mailbox (in the order they were copied), and the UIDs assigned to those messages in the destination mailbox (in the order they were assigned).

This allows a client to track which source messages were copied to which destination UIDs without additional server queries. The response only appears when at least one message was successfully copied.

Example: A003 OK [COPYUID 38505 304,319:320 3956:3958] Done indicates three messages (304, 319, and 320) were copied from the source and assigned UIDs 3956, 3957, and 3958 in the destination mailbox.
sections.plainLanguage: When you copy messages to a different folder, COPYUID tells you which messages you copied and what numbers they got in the new folder. Without this, you would need to look in the new folder to figure out which message is which.

sections.title: Use in Disconnected Clients
sections.content:
UIDPLUS is specifically designed for clients that download messages for offline reading and later sync changes back to the server. These clients must track which local messages correspond to which server UIDs.

When an offline client appends new messages, APPENDUID ensures the client immediately learns the server UIDs assigned to those messages. When copying or moving messages, COPYUID provides the mapping between source and destination UIDs. The UID EXPUNGE command lets the client safely delete messages even if the mailbox was modified between the download and the sync.

The RFC notes that the means of supporting disconnected operation in IMAP was not yet fully documented, and there was no consensus on the best approach. However, UIDPLUS provides useful optimizations for any IMAP client strategy.
sections.plainLanguage: Email programs that work offline need to remember which messages they sent to the server and what the server called them. UIDPLUS helps these programs keep track without needing to ask the server a lot of extra questions.
